items.q: What is AI motion transfer and how does Genjutsu AI work?
items.a: Upload a character image and choose a built-in dance reference. AI applies the reference motion to your character; details and movement can vary.

items.q: How is Genjutsu AI different from generic face swap apps?
items.a: Motion transfer animates the body from a reference performance. It is different from replacing only a face in an existing clip.

items.q: Does it work with anime, 3D avatars, and illustrated art?
items.a: You can use human photos, anime illustrations or 3D character images. Use a clear single character; complex poses and fine details can be less consistent.

items.q: What kind of photos work best?
items.a: Use a clear image showing one character’s head, torso and preferably full body. JPEG, PNG or WebP, at least 320 pixels per side, up to 4 megapixels and 8 MB.

items.q: Can I upload my own custom dance or workout video?
items.a: This release offers two built-in 10-second motion references: Hip-Hop and K-Pop. Custom reference video upload is not available.

items.q: What output format and resolution do I receive?
items.a: A 10-second 720p MP4 based on the selected vertical reference. Music and audio are not guaranteed; add licensed sound when posting if needed.

items.q: What happens if a video render fails?
items.a: Confirmed failures return one credit. If the provider submission is uncertain, support reviews it before resubmitting. Successful renders are not refunded automatically for subjective preferences.

items.q: Do you own the rights to the videos you generate?
items.a: Use images you own or have permission to use, and get the depicted person’s consent. Generated media does not grant rights to third-party characters, music or source material.
